# py-core: PyO3 bindings core (jix-py)

## Purpose

The Python `jix.Array` (`jix-py/src/array.rs:122`) is a `frozen` pyclass holding a type-erased
`ArrayAny` plus a `Mutex<ArrayCache>` (cached numpy dtype + one reusable `ReadContext`). This
subsystem covers: wrapping numpy data as zero-copy `Plain` storage (`ops/common/operand.rs`),
numpy <-> jix dtype mapping (`dtype.rs`), materializing to numpy (`Array.numpy()`, `__getitem__`,
`out=`), basic-index parsing (`ops/shape_ops.rs:206`), `compact`, archive read/write incl. Python
file-like adapters and mmap (`archive.rs`), `errstate` (`error.rs`), helpers (`util.rs`), type-hint
wrappers (`type_hint.rs`) and the Python package shim (`python/jix/__init__.py`).
The module declares free-threading support: pyo3 0.30 `#[pymodule]` defaults `gil_used=false`
(pyo3-macros-backend `module.rs:421`), and release.yaml ships 3.14t/3.15t and 32-bit (x86, armv7, win32) wheels.

## Contracts

Provided to Python callers:
- `Array.numpy(index=None, *, out=None)` (`array.rs:518-632`): returns a numpy array with the
  shape selected by `index`. Without `out` the result is a fresh `PyArray_Empty` allocation laid
  out in the storage's `read_layout_order` (`array.rs:542-551`, `util.rs:102-128`) - NOT always
  C-contiguous. With `out` the same object is returned after `check_output_array`
  (`array.rs:216-286`): dtype `is_equiv_to` the cached numpy dtype, exact shape, `WRITEABLE` flag,
  base pointer and every stride (of dims with extent > 1) aligned to the jix dtype alignment, no
  negative and no zero strides on extent > 1 dims. Empty selections return before any write
  (`array.rs:594-597`).
- `__getitem__` == `numpy(index)` (`array.rs:722`). Index grammar (`shape_ops.rs:206-350`): int,
  `slice` with step 1, `...` (at most one), tuple of these (len <= NDIM_MAX). Ints and slices are
  bounds-checked strictly; trailing dims are filled with full slices; int items drop the dim.
- `jix.asarray(x)` (`ops/as_array.rs:53`): jix Array returned as-is; Python/0-d numpy scalars become a
  `Scalar` storage (value copy, `operand.rs:59-163`); any other input goes through `np.asarray`
  and is wrapped zero-copy as `Plain<Py<PyUntypedArray>>` (`operand.rs:165-197`) that owns a
  strong ref to the numpy object, so the buffer stays alive while any jix view references it
  (doc `as_array.rs:33-38`). `asarray(dtype=)`/`jix.cast` add a lazy cast and cache the
  USER-SUPPLIED numpy descr (`as_array.rs:62-70`, `ops/mod.rs:91-101`).
- `jix.compact` (`array.rs:1597-1618`) always detaches; `resolve_array_params`
  (`array.rs:1620-1718`) rejects unknown keys (TypeError) and unknown codec/filter (ValueError).
- `read_array` / `write_array` (`archive.rs:90-237`): path I/O runs detached; Python file-like I/O
  runs attached through `PyReader`/`PyWriter`. `mmap=True` only for paths.
- Error mapping (`util.rs:54-64`): core `ErrorKind::Arithmetic` -> `FloatingPointError`, every
  other core error -> `RuntimeError` (tests rely on it, e.g. `test_bad_input.py:26`).
- `errstate`/`geterr` (`error.rs`): per-OS-thread modes (`error.rs:19-21`), applied to the
  read context at read time (`array.rs:172`, `error.rs:173-188`); warnings collected in the
  context and emitted as `RuntimeWarning` after the read (`error.rs:190-195`).

Relied on from jix core:
- `ArrayStorage::read_data` / `Array::to_ndarray_buf` push mode writes EVERY element of the
  index region into `out` and nothing else (gap bytes inside the span are untouched; asserted by
  `test_numpy_out.py:53-61`). jix-py discards the returned buffer (`array.rs:624-626`) and hands
  uninitialized `PyArray_Empty` memory to Python, so a hole = uninitialized-memory leak.
- `to_ndarray_buf` only checks `strides.len()==ndim` and writability of `out`
  (`jix/src/storage/buf.rs:282-297`), NOT that the buffer span covers the index region. The
  caller (jix-py) must make `read_shape` equal the index extents and `strides` match.
- `StridedBuf::from_raw_parts_mut` (`buf.rs:84-93`): data valid for the span; "should" have no
  two indices mapping to the same byte. Core is single-threaded (no rayon/threads in `jix/`).
- `spec().read_layout_order()` is a permutation of `0..ndim` (only `debug_assert` on length,
  `util.rs:107`; a duplicate makes `PyArray_Transpose` error, a short list panics at `util.rs:113`).
- `Plain::new` (`jix/src/storage/plain.rs:108-123`): `data` valid for reads at every index of
  `shape` via `strides` for the lifetime of the storage; unaligned data/strides are allowed
  (`plain.rs:97-100`); `strides` are `usize` (negatives must be rejected by caller).
- `read_from_file_mmap` (`jix/src/archive/array.rs:185-191`): UB if the file is modified while
  mapped; jix-py forwards that to users in the docstring (`archive.rs:35-38`).

Safety arguments of unsafe blocks (who establishes them):
- `array.rs:603-608` `&mut [u8]` over the destination: numpy guarantees its own view is in
  bounds; span from `strided_span_bytes` with numpy strides (non-dropped dims) and synthetic
  C-order strides for dropped/extent-1 dims (`array.rs:563-592`). Exclusivity vs. source buffers
  is NOT checked: documented UB if `out` overlaps an `asarray` source (`array.rs:467-485`).
- `array.rs:616-623` `StridedBuf::from_raw_parts_mut`: no-alias established only by
  `check_output_array` (zero/negative strides); self-overlapping positive strides not checked.
- `operand.rs:181,185-194` `Plain::new`: keep-alive by storing `array.unbind()` in the storage;
  read validity by numpy's own invariants; negative strides rejected (`operand.rs:172-179`).
- `archive.rs:122-125` mmap: user contract (docstring).
- `archive.rs:417-427` `PyMemoryView_FromMemory` over `buf`: sound only if Python `write()`
  keeps no reference/slice/export past the call (comment `archive.rs:409-416`); enforced only by
  `release()` whose error is discarded (`archive.rs:437`).

| `util.rs:88-97` `PyArray_Empty` + `cast_into_unchecked` | descr ref is stolen (`into_dtype_ptr`), result is ndarray | local; dims cast `u64 as npy_intp` unchecked (`util.rs:86`) |
| `util.rs:124-127` `PyArray_Transpose` | `permute` is a permutation of ndim | caller (`read_layout_order`), numpy re-validates |
| `util.rs:143-152` `PyArray_Newshape` | - | dead code (`#[allow(unused)]`) |
| `util.rs:308-321` `UnsafeSend` (unconditional `Send`) | caller-justified `unsafe fn new` | dead code: no call sites |
| `util.rs:362-404` `array_try_from_fn` (MaybeUninit, InitGuard) | each slot written once; guard drops `[0..initialized)` | local |
| `util.rs:408-445` `array_try_map` (ptr::read + DropGuard) | each src read once; guard drops `src[next..]` | local; `next` set before `f` runs |

| `array.rs:603-608`, `616-623` | see Contracts | `check_output_array` / fresh allocation; NON-LOCAL (index parse, stride rebuild, numpy dims) |
| `operand.rs:181`, `185-194` | Plain::new contract | numpy invariants + keep-alive; Python-side behavior (resize refcheck=False, as_strided, concurrent writers) can break it |
| `archive.rs:122-125` | file not modified | user (documented) |
| `archive.rs:417-427` | Python `write()` does not retain the view | Python-side behavior; only partially enforced |

Flagged as depending on non-local or Python-side behavior: `array.rs:603-623` (correctness of
`parse_basic_index`, `read_layout_order`, numpy's dim expansion of subarray descrs, 32-bit
casts), `operand.rs:185` (numpy buffer not resized/freed/mutated concurrently while the GIL is
released in `numpy()`/`compact`/`write_array`), `archive.rs:417`.

## Edge-case surface

- Negative strides: rejected for inputs (`operand.rs:172-179`, even on extent<=1 dims); for `out`
  only on extent>1 dims (`array.rs:268`, extent<=1 handled at `array.rs:575-588`).
- Non-contiguous / Fortran / gapped / transposed `out`: supported (`test_numpy_out.py:24-51`).
  Self-overlapping `as_strided` out (e.g. strides (8,8) on int64) passes the checks.
- Read-only `out`: rejected via `NPY_ARRAY_WRITEABLE` (`array.rs:246`). Read-only inputs: fine (Plain only reads).
- Unaligned numpy inputs (packed struct field views, `frombuffer(offset=1)`): accepted by Plain;
  unaligned `out`: rejected (`array.rs:259-284`).
- Byte order: `dtype_from_numpy` only matches `(kind, itemsize)` (`dtype.rs:138-176`); `'>i4'` maps to I32.
- Struct dtypes: only packed or aligned layouts (`jix/src/dtype.rs:611-619`); object/str/void/
  datetime fields rejected recursively (`dtype.rs:168-175,197`); Itemsize/offsets must fit `Itemsize`.
- Subarray dtypes: numpy never yields them at array top level, but `dtype_sub_field` on a field
  like `('a','i4',(3,))` produces a jix Array whose dtype has an inner shape; `dtype_to_numpy`
  returns a subarray descr (`dtype.rs:75-76`) that `PyArray_Empty` expands into extra dims.
- 0-d: `a[()]`/`a[...]` return a 0-d ndarray (never a numpy scalar); `item()` requires ndim 0
  (`array.rs:653-661`); `__len__` on 0-d raises ValueError (`array.rs:376-383`).
- Python ints: index items via `extract::<i64>` (overflow surfaces as TypeError,
  `shape_ops.rs:245-250`); Python `bool` passes as 0/1; dims via `i32`; `repeats: u64`;
  `offset/len: u64`; scalars > u64 become f64 (`operand.rs:64-72`).
- Slices: `slice_unpack` (`util.rs:19-34`) maps an omitted (or >= Py_ssize_t::MAX) stop to the
  dim length, so `a[0:2**70]` is silently accepted; start must satisfy `start < len`
  (`shape_ops.rs:314`). On 32-bit `length as Py_ssize_t` truncates.
- 32-bit targets: `(end-start) as usize` (`array.rs:529`), `u64 as npy_intp` (`util.rs:86`),
  `*len as usize` (`array.rs:382`), `size()` product (`array.rs:358`).
- mmap: file truncated/overwritten while mapped is UB/SIGBUS (documented); unlink is fine on POSIX.
- GIL release: `numpy()` detaches unless the storage is `plain_read` AND <= 4096 bytes
  (`array.rs:610-611`); `compact` and path read/write always detach. Concurrent Python writers
  to an asarray-wrapped buffer or to `out` are data races (NumPy-like semantics, undocumented).
- Deep lazy chains (`for _ in range(10**6): a = a + 1`): Arc drop / read recursion depth is
  unbounded on the Rust side.

## Intentional behaviors (do not report)

- `out` aliasing a buffer the array reads (via `asarray`) is documented UB (`array.rs:467-485`).
- Strict bounds, step must be 1, no `None`/newaxis/fancy/bool-array indexing (`array.rs:444-448`,
  `array.rs:493-500`, `docs/module.md:96`, `test_slice.py:212-263`).
- Negative-stride inputs raise ValueError (`as_array.rs:43`, `array.rs:1566-1569`,
  `test_bad_input.py:99-102`); reversed/broadcast/read-only `out` raise ValueError
  (`test_numpy_out.py:243-265`); reversed length-1 `out` dim accepted (`test_getitem.py:129-137`).
- `out` must be aligned even though core does not require it (`array.rs:255-263`, `array.rs:463`).
- `__bool__` always raises (`array.rs:385-396`); `__pos__` rejects bool/struct (`array.rs:982-1001`);
  `pow(a, b, mod)` raises NotImplementedError (`array.rs:950-955`); `item()` only for ndim 0.
- `errstate` applies on call, not on `__enter__`; per thread; modes in effect at READ time apply;
  defaults `raise` for divide/invalid (`error.rs:38-51`, `test_errstate.py:123-182`).
- Non-arithmetic core errors surface as RuntimeError (`test_bad_input.py:25-27,148-155`).
- `read_array` default validation is `strict` (`archive.rs:42`); offset/mmap unsupported for
  file-likes (`archive.rs:130-139`); `write_array` without `append` uses `create_new`
  (`archive.rs:212-213`, `test_archive.py:43`); `append` ignored for file-likes.
- `write()` returning None counts as a full write; `read()` returning None is EOF; over-reporting
  raises (`archive.rs:306-307,439-449`, `test_bad_input.py:148-155`).
- A stashed (unsliced) memoryview becomes a released view after `write` (`archive.rs:769` test).
- Python aliases `jix.pow/abs/concat/clip/prod/sub/mul/div/neg` shadow builtins on purpose
  (`python/jix/__init__.py:9-34`).

### Changed since generation (dbb99e2 #85, 5b3a9f5 #86) - these supersede conflicting bullets above
- A dtype mismatch raises TypeError (was RuntimeError); see the py-ops doc for the op-level
  changes (unsigned negate, Python ints outside int64 raise OverflowError, broadcast inserts dims).
- jix-py/src/archive.rs and array.rs were reworked (archive.rs ~50 lines); re-read them rather
  than trusting line numbers here.
- `resolve_array_params` uses `try_block_shape` / `try_block_shape_fixed_dims` (no panic on > 8 dims).
- mmap reads check section bounds against the mapped file (KNOWN K5, fixed).
Line numbers in this doc refer to bb1ee2c.

### Changed in c009869 (#87) - supersedes conflicting statements above (line numbers above refer to bb1ee2c)
- Big-endian numpy dtypes raise. A Python bool index raises. `Array.__array_ufunc__ = None`, so a
  numpy operand on the left defers to jix's reflected op. numpy() documents its memory order as
  implementation-defined, and that out= must not overlap any numpy array in the lazy chain.

### Changed in 6f8e220 (#88) and 7e93487 (#89) - supersedes conflicting statements above
- #89: numpy bool arrays map to `bool8` and are wrapped zero-copy with any byte values (K15 fixed);
  results come back as numpy bool. #88: numpy structured dtypes with padding are rejected
  (jix-py/src/dtype.rs reworked, test_struct_dtype.py added).

### Changed in 4d11918 (#90) - supersedes conflicting statements above
- write_array rejects append-mode files and no longer lists gzip.GzipFile as supported (K49, K57).

### Changed in 691e11b (#91) - supersedes conflicting statements above
- `Array.numpy()` of a dtype with an inner shape allocates the base dtype with the inner dims
  appended to the shape, and takes the array's strides from the first `ndim` numpy dims.
  `numpy(out=)` must have those trailing inner dims, C-contiguous (`check_output_array`) (K66).
- Operand inputs accept any stride, negative included, on a dim of length <= 1 (operand.rs:171-178)
  (K80). This supersedes the "negative strides rejected even on extent<=1 dims" statements above.

## Hot spots

- Stride rebuild in `numpy()` (`array.rs:563-592`): it pops `np_arr.strides()` from the end
  assuming `np_arr.ndim == out_shape.len()`. When can numpy hand back a different ndim (subarray
  descr) or strides that do not cover `read_shape`?
- Can any path give `to_ndarray_buf` an `out` smaller than the index region (32-bit casts,
  `read_shape` vs `index` divergence, dropped-dim synthetic strides)? `check_out_buf` will not catch it.
- Cached numpy dtype (`ArrayCache.numpy_dtype`) vs `arr.dtype()`: `from_core_with_np_dtype`
  callers (`as_array.rs:68`, `ops/mod.rs:100`, `shape_ops.rs:103..1230`, `where_op.rs:79`) must
  only cache a descr with identical memory layout. Which numpy descrs map to a jix dtype but have
  a different layout (byte order, align flag, subarray)?
- `numpy_dtype()` (`array.rs:288-298`) holds a `std::sync::Mutex` while calling Python
  (`dtype_to_numpy` imports numpy and calls `numpy.dtype(..., align=True)`); `read_ctx`
  (`array.rs:163-177`) and `ContextGuard::drop` (`array.rs:1724-1730`) lock it from attached threads.
- `parse_basic_index`: zero-length dims, `start == len`, `True`/`np.bool_`, `-0`, huge ints,
  ellipsis plus ints filling exactly `ndim`.
- Free-threaded: `&mut [u8]` over `out` and `&[u8]` over Plain sources live across `py.detach`;
  other threads can mutate/reshape (`.shape=`, `.strides=`) the same ndarrays meanwhile.
- `PyWriter::write`: which Python operations on the memoryview survive `release()`?
- `array_try_map`/`array_try_from_fn`: panic in `f` mid-way; `T` needs drop but `U` does not.
- Recent churn (`git log -15 -- jix-py/src`): #76 errstate/warnings plumbing (`error.rs`,
  `read_ctx`, `emit_warnings`), #82/#84 dtype promotion and np-dtype caching in
  where/stack/concatenate, #73 pyo3 0.30 + type_hint wrappers, #75 removal of `D: Dimension`
  (index/stride code in `numpy()`), #52 `read_layout_order` allocation.

### Suspicions (unverified)

- `jix-py/src/dtype.rs:138` - byte order never checked (`is_native_byteorder` unused): `'>i4'` data is wrapped zero-copy (`operand.rs:184`) and read as little-endian; `asarray(x, dtype='>f8')`/`cast` cache a big-endian descr so `numpy()` writes LE bytes into a BE-labeled array.
- `jix-py/src/array.rs:551` - a jix dtype with inner shape (via `dtype_sub_field` on a subarray field) yields a subarray descr; `PyArray_Empty` appends the inner dims, so the reversed-stride walk at `array.rs:564-574` assigns inner strides to outer dims (overlapping writes, uninitialized output) or the transpose fails.
- `jix-py/src/ops/shape_ops.rs:314` - `start_norm >= len` rejects valid empty slices with start == len (`a[3:3]` on len 3, `a[:]`/`a[0:0]` on a zero-length dim), contradicting `array.rs:446`.
- `jix-py/src/ops/shape_ops.rs:245` - Python `bool` index is accepted as int, so `a[True]` returns row 1 instead of NumPy's mask semantics.
- `jix-py/src/util.rs:185-192` - `normalize_dims` collects an unbounded slice into `ArrayVec<_, 8>`; `permute_dims` passes an unbounded `Vec<i32>` (`shape_ops.rs:599,606`, `array.rs:1265`) so 9+ dims panic (PanicException) instead of ValueError.
- `jix-py/src/array.rs:529` - (32-bit wheels) `u64 as usize` and `u64 as npy_intp` (`util.rs:86`) wrap for a dim >= 2^32 (e.g. `jix.broadcast(x, (2**32+4,))`), numpy allocates a small buffer while `to_ndarray_buf` receives the full index range: possible heap overflow.
- `jix-py/src/array.rs:264-284` - `out` stride checks do not reject self-overlapping positive strides or stride < itemsize (as_strided), violating `StridedBuf::from_raw_parts_mut`'s no-alias requirement (`jix/src/storage/buf.rs:81-82`).
- `jix-py/src/archive.rs:437` - `memoryview.release()` errors are ignored; a slice (`mv[1:]`) or buffer export (`np.frombuffer(mv)`) taken in a user `write()` outlives `buf` - use-after-free reachable from safe Python (only acknowledged in a code comment).
- `jix-py/src/array.rs:289-297` - Mutex held across Python calls; a second thread blocking on it while attached (free-threaded stop-the-world, or GIL handoff during GC in `dtype_to_numpy`) can deadlock.
- `jix-py/src/dtype.rs:208-211` - debug_assert fails for a non-aligned numpy struct whose fields all have alignment 1 (core classifies it aligned, `jix/src/dtype.rs:653-676`): panic in debug builds.
- `jix-py/src/array.rs:489-491` - docstring promises a C-contiguous result, but allocation follows `read_layout_order` (`array.rs:542-551`), e.g. F-order for `asarray` of a Fortran array.
- `jix-py/src/ops/common/operand.rs:176` - negative stride rejected even on extent<=1 dims (`np.arange(1)[::-1]`), unlike the `out=` path.
